title: Grade 6, moving up from Grade 7
summary: Moving from Grade 7 to Grade 6: leading a large area of work and its senior managers, owning outcomes, budgets and risks across teams, and advising directors. This route builds the leadership, delivery and public-money knowledge and the examples that Grade 6 adverts ask for.

areas.label: Behaviours and evidence at Grade 6
areas.why: Show Leadership, Seeing the Big Picture and Making Effective Decisions at the next grade.

areas.label: Leading leaders and influencing
areas.why: Briefing senior leaders, handling disagreement and leading through change.

areas.label: Leading managers and building teams
areas.why: Setting direction, developing managers and handling performance across teams.

areas.label: Delivering across teams
areas.why: Owning a plan, dependencies and results across several teams.

areas.label: Budgets and financial judgement
areas.why: Owning a significant budget, forecasts and value for money.

areas.label: Risk and resilience
areas.why: Seeing the big risks and keeping services running.

areas.label: Business cases and public money
areas.why: The Green Book, options appraisal and managing public money.

areas.label: Governance and assurance
areas.why: Accountability, assurance and scrutiny of public spending.

stages.label: Understand the next grade
stages.blurb: Read the Grade 6 role profile and agree what evidence you need.

stages.label: Build the skills and evidence
stages.blurb: Build leadership, delivery and public-money skills at the next level.

stages.label: Show it and apply
stages.blurb: Use the evidence in applications and interviews.

actions.label: Read two Grade 6 adverts and their role profiles
actions.detail: Note the Behaviours, the size of area and budget, and what is assessed at each stage.

actions.label: Find a senior sponsor or mentor
actions.detail: Ask a Grade 6 or SCS colleague to review your evidence and tell you honestly where you fall short.

actions.label: Write six examples at Grade 6 level
actions.detail: Cover leading change across teams, managing a budget, handling a serious risk, influencing a director, developing a manager and an improvement with a measured result.

actions.label: Take on a cross-team piece of work
actions.detail: Lead or deputise on something that spans teams, so your examples are about scale and leadership.

actions.label: Practise a Grade 6 panel interview out loud
actions.detail: Include a presentation if the advert asks for one, with a colleague asking hard questions.

apply.label: Apply for Grade 6 vacancies
apply.detail: Apply to Grade 6 roles as they appear, including temporary promotions and cross-department moves. Ask for feedback after every result.
